summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with bash, git, and curl, then installs fzf (a fuzzy finder tool) to make searching through files and command history interactive. It sets up a demo directory structure with sample log files and pre-populates bash history so users can immediately practice fuzzy searching when the container starts.

explanations.3: This tells Docker to skip interactive prompts during package installation, since a container can't respond to user input.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag installs only the packages you explicitly ask for, skipping optional dependencies to keep the image smaller.
explanations.11: After installing packages, this deletes the package cache that apt-get downloads, freeing up disk space since we won't need to reinstall those same packages.
explanations.15: The install script wires fzf's keyboard shortcuts (like Ctrl+T) directly into bash, but --no-update-rc prevents it from modifying .bashrc automatically since we'll do that manually in the next line.
explanations.16: This manually adds fzf's bash initialization to .bashrc so the fuzzy-finder features are available every time the shell starts.
explanations.22: The printf command creates a multi-line log file for each iteration; $i is replaced with the loop counter (1, 2, 3, 4) to create four different log files.
explanations.30: printf with %s prints each line followed by a newline, building a fake command history that looks like real commands a user typed.
explanations.41: This adds a custom shell prompt that shows a whale emoji and username in yellow/cyan colors, making it visually obvious you're inside a container.
explanations.43: The -i flag runs bash in interactive mode even though there's no terminal attached, so you get a working shell prompt when you run the container.
